article.body_html:
The moment you realise the bike will reach the shop late is the moment for one short phone call, not for riding faster. Extra time is priced by the hour and steps up after six hours, so find out early what you will be charged. Below: what to say, what the shop's confirmed extension fee comes to hour by hour, and the questions worth asking while the shop is still on the line.

Call first, and keep the call short

Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà is open 09:00–21:00 daily at Ngõ 5 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội (near Gia Lâm bus station). Phone: 0334 699 969. Pull over somewhere safe before you call; a rider who negotiates with one hand on the bars is a bigger risk than the delay.

In about thirty seconds, give the shop five things:

  • your name and which bike you have;
  • the return time you agreed;
  • when you now expect to arrive, with a margin: "between 19:30 and 20:00" is more useful than one exact time you may miss;
  • roughly where you are;
  • one question: how will the extra time be charged?

If the shop reads messages, the same content works in writing, for example: "This is [your name]. I have the scooter I rented today and I am stuck in traffic. We agreed 18:00 and I now expect to arrive between 19:30 and 20:00. How will the extra time be charged?" Send it only after you have stopped, and ask the shop which channel it prefers rather than assuming one.

What extra time costs under the confirmed extension fee

The shop's confirmed extension fee is 20,000 VND per hour, and more than 6 hours is charged as one rental day. If the shop bills a late return the same way, that gives a simple price curve; ask whether it does. The table uses whole hours; how part of an hour is charged is one of the questions below.

Hours lateExtension fee
1 hour20,000 VND
2 hours40,000 VND
3 hours60,000 VND
4 hours80,000 VND
5 hours100,000 VND
6 hours120,000 VND
More than 6 hoursOne rental day

The reference price of one day for a manual or automatic bike is 150,000 to 200,000 VND; the exact figure for your bike has to be confirmed when you book. Set beside the 120,000 VND of six hours, the step from the sixth hour to the seventh adds about 30,000 to 80,000 VND, more than the 20,000 VND of an ordinary hour. Being five hours late and being seven hours late are therefore different kinds of cost, and the jump is the reason to know early which side of it you will land on.

Two worked examples

  • A traffic jam on the way back. You agreed to return at 18:00 and arrive at 20:15, two hours and fifteen minutes late. Counted in full hours that is 40,000 VND; if a started hour counts, it is 60,000 VND. The 20,000 VND between the two answers is exactly one hour of the fee, which is why the partial-hour question is worth asking.
  • The bike is still out when the shop closes. You agreed to return at 14:30, the day trip overran and you reach the shop at 21:30: seven hours late and half an hour after closing time. That is more than 6 hours, so the rule gives one rental day. The rule does not say what happens to a bike that arrives after 21:00, so that is a question for the call, not an assumption.

Questions to ask while you are on the phone

  • Does the extra time start at the time we agreed, or at some other point?
  • How is part of an hour charged: rounded up, or counted as it is?
  • If I arrive after 21:00, what should I do with the bike and the keys, and when will the return be recorded?
  • Can you tell me the extra amount now, so that we both expect the same figure at the counter?

Write down the answers with the time of the call and the name of the person you spoke to. If the shop confirms the new return time in writing, keep that; if it only says it by phone, a note of the time, the person and the figure is still better than memory. Until the shop agrees, do not leave the bike outside a closed shop or hand the keys to anyone else.

Use the extra minutes safely

Riding faster to save one hour of 20,000 VND is a poor trade, and so is skipping a rest because you are behind schedule. The table gives you a price to plan around; a mistake at speed has no table. If you are already tired, the guide to rest stops and a return cutoff on a day trip explains how to choose the time after which you stop adding stops. If the delay comes from a breakdown rather than traffic, photograph the bike and the place it stopped, and call the shop before you arrange any repair.

If you will be more than six hours late whatever you do, hurrying will not change the last row of the table, so ride at a normal pace and call again if your arrival time changes. Ask the shop whether that day is counted from the agreed return time.

At the counter

When you arrive, compare the extra charge with the figure you were given, ask for the return to be recorded with the real time, and ask for a receipt or a written note. Returning a Rental Motorbike in Hanoi: A Receipt and Handover Checklist lists what a receipt should show. For staying longer on purpose rather than by accident, see how to extend your rental period, and for how pickup and return work at the shop, the delivery and pickup guide. If you want the whole set of return guides in one place, open the Delivery & Return Planning category.
